what: lane RS asked at 15:36 for step 1 of `blaze run`'s live line; the queue held 13 requests and the runner had a `stop` file since 15:19, so nothing was served. `ask` says only 'N request(s) ahead of it' and then waits up to 50 minutes in silence; the Bash tool moved it to the background after 180 s, with its output piped through tail, so nothing showed that the queue was stopped.
cost: about 20 minutes spent waiting and reading the queue's folder to find the stop file
cause: ask does not look for the runner's stop file before it waits
whys: the stop is the coordinator's switch, and a lane cannot see it from the ask's words
class: a wait on a server that is not serving, with nothing saying so
prevention: wanted: ask prints 'the runner is stopped (runner/stop since HH:MM): your request stays filed' and exits at once when the stop file is there
annoyance: no word that the runner is stopped; the request stays filed after the ask is stopped, so a later serve of it is answered to no one
workaround: read runner/stop and runner/log.md; stop the ask; go on writing; ask again once it serves
